To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rigid microenvironments promote the differentiation of cardiomyocytes.
the stiffness of the extracellular matrix can promote the production of functional cardiac tissue from embryonic stem cells.
the stiffness of the extracellular matrix influences the yield of de novo cardiac differentiation from pluripotent embryonic stem cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of extracellular stiffness on stem cell differentiation and function.
the role of matrix stiffness on the cardiac differentiation of embryonic stem cells and the subsequent maturation of these cells.
the role of matrix stiffness on cardiac differentiation from embryonic stem (es) cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

matrix rigidity is an important factor that influences the induction of cardiogenic cells from pluripotent ES cells and that the rigidity of the matrix influences the maturation and synchronization of cardiomyocytes.
the rigidity of the extracellular micro environment plays an important role in the differentiation and maturation of cardiomyocytes.
the matrix stiffness is a crucial factor in the cardiac differentiation of mouse or human embryonic stem cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rigidity of the matrix environment can promote the differentiation of cardiomyocytes, and the rigidity of this microenvironment is an independent factor that can instruct not only the matuation of already differentiated cardiocytes, but also the induction of cardiocytes from undifferentiated cells.
we have identified that rigid matrices promote the differentiation of ES cells to cardiomyocytes.
we demonstrate that rigid microenvironments promote cardiac specification of mouse and human ES cell derived cardiomyocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stiffness of the microenvironment is a key factor in promoting cardiomyocyte differentiation from embryonic stem (or induced pluripotent stem) cells.
the rigidity of the extracellular matrix can influence the differentiation of stem cells into specific cell types, in this case cardiomyocytes.
the stiffness of the extracellular matrix (ECM) can be manipulated to influence the differentiation and maturation of cardiomyocytes.
